Content: The information below is about ways that early cultures measured the passage of time.

:box:Observing the `text(Sun)`, the `text(Moon)`, the planets, and the stars has helped people measure the passage of time since the prehistoric era. By carefully recording the movement of heavenly bodies across the sky, ancient peoples could keep track of the change in seasons and the passing of months and years.

While we have no direct knowledge of how timekeeping developed, historians have found evidence of it in many parts of the world. The earliest evidence is from the Ice Age. It consists of sticks and bones with marks on them. These items may have been used to keep track of the days between moon phases.

Early civilizations in Mesopotamia had a calendar similar to our own. The Egyptians had a calendar that allowed them to know when the flooding of the Nile began. At Stonehenge in England, the stones are aligned to determine the timing of solstices, which marked the change of seasons. These examples and many more have shown historians that the accurate measurement of time was an important development.
Based on this information, what was a `bbtext(main)` purpose of the Egyptian calendar?

A.Choice: to schedule when to start military conquests

B.Choice: to plan the building of royal pyramids

C.Choice: to decide when to elect pharaohs

D.Choice: to know when to plant crops

SubTopics: Summarize the breakup of the Kingdom of Israel, Babylonian captivity, and the return of the Jews to their homeland under the Persian Empire.
Content: The passage below discusses events after the breakup of ancient Israel into `text(two)` kingdoms.

:box:The Kingdom of Israel became two separate kingdoms. `text(Ten)` of the `text(twelve)` Hebrew tribes stayed in the northern part of the old kingdom. They kept the name the Kingdom of Israel. The other `text(two)` Hebrew tribes established the Kingdom of Judah in the region to the south that included the city of Jerusalem.

The northern Kingdom of Israel lasted about `250` `text(years)` before it was conquered by the Assyrians. The Assyrians then broke up the ten tribes that lived in the kingdom and made them depart from their homeland. As was their practice, the Assyrians scattered the former residents of the Kingdom of Israel across their territory.

Unlike the Kingdom of Israel, the Kingdom of Judah successfully defended itself from the Assyrian conquests. It lasted about another `150` `text(years)` before it was conquered by Nebuchadnezzar, the king of the Babylonians. When the Babylonians captured the Kingdom of Judah, they took over Jerusalem, destroyed the temple, and resettled many Jews in their homeland of Mesopotamia. They made Judah a province of their territory, which ended the political freedom of the Jewish people.

About `30` `text(years)` later, the Persians invaded the region and captured it from the Babylonians. Although he kept possession of the region, the Persian ruler, Cyrus the Great, allowed the Jews that had been removed from their homeland to return there. He also allowed them to rebuild their temple. The Jews lived for the next `text(two centuries)` under Persian rule.
Which statement explains how the Persians' conquest of Jewish territory was different from that of the other empires?

A.Choice: The Persians allowed the Jews to keep their political independence.

B.Choice: The Persians allowed the Jews to preserve their cultural heritage.

C.Choice: The Persians forced the Jews to reunite their kingdoms.

D.Choice: The Persians forced the Jews to leave their kingdoms.

:box:Geography provided ancient Greece with a unique physical setting. Being on a peninsula allowed every part of Greece to be near the sea. The irregular coastline and nearby islands offered many sheltered harbors. Short mountain ranges divided the interior into small sections. Greece also had a mild climate and plenty of rainfall.
